open_points.subject: object-folder input contract
open_points.question: What information counts as file metadata at this boundary, including its fields, types, availability and distinction from metadata embedded in image bytes?
options: Only size and modification time
Filesystem stat data including type, size, times and permissions
Extended attributes and link information as well
Image metadata such as EXIF
open_points.default_guess: Filesystem entry type, byte size and modification time only

open_points.subject: use of file metadata
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: Which delivery decisions may depend on metadata, and which metadata fields, if any, contribute to source identity, eligibility, content-change detection or image preparation?
options: Metadata is diagnostic only
Metadata affects eligibility and safety checks but not identity
Metadata contributes to source identity and change detection
Metadata may also alter image preparation
open_points.default_guess: Use entry type and size for safety checks and use a byte digest, not metadata, for identity and content-change detection

witness.initial: A confirmed project contains a file whose name and bytes stay unchanged while its modification time changes.
events: Syncthing-fork changes only the file's modification time.
Calling flow asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The deliverer returns the same source id and status because metadata does not define identity.
The deliverer returns a new source id or ready state because metadata participates in identity or change detection.

open_points.subject: consistency of folder reads
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: What consistency must hold between a file's name, metadata and bytes when Syncthing replaces or modifies it during a read?
options: Use each value whenever it is read
Require matching metadata before and after reading the bytes
Open one stable file handle and validate its identity
Reject any entry observed changing and retry only on a later request
open_points.default_guess: Read through one handle, compare identity, size and modification data before and after, and reject the entry if they changed

witness.initial: A confirmed folder contains photo.jpg with metadata M1 and bytes B1.
events: Calling flow asks what can be delivered or asks for placement.
Syncthing-fork replaces photo.jpg with metadata M2 and bytes B2 while the deliverer is reading it.
outcomes: The deliverer accepts a mixed observation such as M1 with B2.
The deliverer rejects the changing file without placing it.

open_points.subject: invalid metadata handling
open_points.question: What happens when metadata is unreadable, unsupported, malformed or changes during inspection: is that file rejected, is the whole project request refused, or is the metadata ignored?
options: Reject only the affected file with a reason
Refuse the entire request without changes
Ignore unusable metadata and continue from the bytes
Retry metadata reads before rejecting
open_points.default_guess: Reject only the affected file with a stable reason and leave other files available

witness.initial: A confirmed project contains one valid photo and one entry whose metadata cannot be read.
events: Calling flow asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The valid photo is returned and the bad entry is rejected with a reason.
The entire request is refused as an unavailable folder or metadata error.

open_points.subject: rejected listing entries
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does a rejected file also carry its source id, and is rejected itself a status or a separate result shape?
options: Every entry, including rejected, has a source id and status
Rejected entries have a reason but no source id
Rejected entries have a source id only when identity could be established
open_points.default_guess: Every identifiable file has a source id; an unidentifiable entry is rejected using its file name and reason

witness.initial: A confirmed project contains a file that is identifiable but cannot be delivered.
events: Calling flow asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The response contains status rejected, the source id and the reason.
The response contains only a rejected result and reason, without the source id.

open_points.subject: placement transaction
open_points.question: What exact writes and state transition constitute a placement, and at what commit point may the deliverer report that placement succeeded?
options: Writing the prepared binary alone is placement
Writing the binary and creating its stable reference together is placement
Binary, reference and publication body must commit atomically
Placement may leave recoverable temporary artifacts before commit
open_points.default_guess: Placement commits only when the prepared binary and stable reference are both durable; temporary artifacts are not placements and must not be externally visible

open_points.subject: failed delivery side effects
open_points.text: a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and no placement is made
open_points.question: Besides forbidding a placement, what state changes or writes are permitted on a failed delivery, including temporary files, rejection records, caches, counters and changes to an earlier placement?
options: No durable state or Portal-store write is permitted
Diagnostic or rejection state may be written but Portal-store content may not
Temporary Portal-store objects may be written if removed before returning
An earlier placement may be retained but never changed or removed
open_points.default_guess: Permit only non-product operational logging; make no durable product-state or Portal-store change and preserve any earlier placement

witness.initial: A source already has a successful placement, and a later delivery request for it cannot be completed.
events: The deliverer detects the failure and reports its reason.
Calling flow later asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The earlier placement remains unchanged and no failure state was stored.
The earlier placement remains, but a durable rejection or attempt record changes the later reported state or reason.
